transcript.text: If your tumble dryer is running continuously and won't stop even when the programme should be finished, this usually points to an electrical fault where the control board has 'stuck' or the timer mechanism is failing. Before we look at parts, please try a full power reset: switch it off at the wall socket (or unplug it) for about 5 minutes to let the electronics discharge, then plug it back in and start a cycle. Does it stop correctly after this reset, or does it keep running?
its not running all the time, only turns for a few seconds every couple of minutes after it says End. dries the clothes fine. should i still unplug it?

Yes, please unplug it for 5 minutes as suggested; this is safe and often clears temporary electronic glitches. The pattern you describe—drying fine but pausing every few minutes—is very typical of a condenser or heat-pump dryer that has filled its water container and cannot drain the remaining condensate. The machine stops heating to protect itself until the pump moves the water, then runs again. Please check if the water tank is full after your next cycle, and listen for a humming sound from the base when it restarts; this will tell us if the pump is working or if the float switch is stuck.
ok. its not stopping to heat though, the clothes are cool and it only turns a little after End. not sure where the water tank is, how do i check?

The water tank is typically a rectangular drawer at the bottom right or left of the front panel. Pull it out gently: if it has a lid that opens to pour, empty it and check the float inside (a small plastic ball) moves freely. If it's a screw-top bottle, unscrew and empty it. Was it full of water, or was it already empty?
i havent found the tank yet, where is it exactly? the dryer is a Beko if that helps

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. On Beko condenser dryers, the water tank is usually located at the bottom right of the front panel; you may need to remove a small plastic cover or grille to access the drawer. However, since your clothes are coming out cool and the machine isn't heating properly, this points more strongly to an airflow restriction than just a full tank. Please check the lint filter in the door opening and the condenser unit behind the bottom flap at the front; if either is clogged with fluff, it can cause the dryer to overheat and cut power intermittently. Clean both thoroughly under a tap (let them dry completely before refitting) and try a cycle again.
the clothes do dry fine though, its just the turning after End. will cleaning those stop it? i dont know where the condenser is either

Cleaning the filters will help efficiency but won't fix the post-cycle turning if the issue is water-related. Since your Beko condenses water into a tank, that 'turning on and off' after End is often the pump trying to move remaining condensate from the base sump into the tank. If the pump is blocked or failing, it may cycle intermittently even when dry. To check this safely: switch the dryer off and unplug it, then tilt it back slightly (get help if needed) to look at the bottom front grille; listen for a hum when you plug it in briefly just to start a drain phase, or simply tell me if you hear that noise during the pauses.
i dont want to tip it back, its heavy. the sound is just the drum turning a few seconds, no humming. it stops when i open the door. any other ideas?

Since the clothes are cool and the drum only turns briefly after 'End', this suggests the machine is likely trying to run a final draining phase but cannot complete it because the pump is blocked or failing. On Beko condenser dryers, there is usually a small access panel at the bottom right of the front; behind it is the drain pump filter. Please unplug the dryer first, then remove that cover and check if the filter is clogged with fluff or debris. If it is clear but the machine still behaves this way, the pump motor itself may be faulty.
ive unplugged it before but not sure which cover you mean. the manual says something about anti-crease, what is that?

The 'anti-crease' feature is a normal part of most dryers designed to prevent your clothes from getting creased while they sit in the drum after the cycle finishes. It works by turning the drum for a few seconds every couple of minutes until you open the door or remove the laundry. Since your dryer dries the clothes fine and only turns briefly at this stage, this is exactly what it should be doing; there is no fault to fix here.
